messages:

Cc: Anika Verma <anika@brightbay.com>

Subject: Production spike — 5xx errors + latency (BrightBay)

Evelyn / Sean —

We just observed a major production outage window in our BrightBay environment between 08:58 and 10:45 PST. Symptoms: sustained 95th/99th percentile latency spikes (token latency up ~4x), elevated 5xx rates across generation endpoints (~12% of requests), and a visible drop in throughput for our peak checkout flows. Our monitoring shows requests queuing and some retries failing.

Attached are our client-side traces and a small sampling of failing request IDs (see stack-trace-20260710.log). This is causing checkout delays for customers in West US, and our ops team is escalating to execs — they want an RCA and a timeline for permanent mitigation.

Can you confirm you received this and what immediate mitigations/redlines you have in flight? We need an exec summary (one pager) and a proposed action plan with owners.

-Jason
Jason Liu

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Production spike — 5xx errors + latency (BrightBay) — preliminary findings

Folks — quick technical update (preliminary):

Timeline (preliminary):
- 08:56 PST — small memory pressure events observed on kv-cache-aggregator processes (node pool bb-prod-1).
- 09:02 PST — LB started rebalancing ~30% of traffic; a subset of nodes hit kernel OOMs during GC, causing process restarts and a transient backlog.
- 09:10–09:45 PST — elevated request queues, retries, and 5xx responses (majority 503/504).
- 09:46 PST — we rolled a config change to reduce cache_size and restarted affected nodes.
- 10:02 PST — traffic normalized; 99th percentile latency returned to baseline by ~10:30 PST.

Root cause (prelim): a memory regression introduced by a recent kv-cache aggregator change (v2.3.1 -> v2.3.2) combined with LB reconfiguration that caused an uneven traffic distribution. The regression increases memory churn during token streaming hot paths; when coupled with GC behavior on our chosen instance type it resulted in kernel-level OOMs.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Reverted the kv-cache aggregator to v2.3.1 across the BrightBay pool (Marcus executed).
- Forced draining of affected nodes, restarted with conservative cache_size setting.
- Applied temporary routing policy to prioritize checkout-related routes.

Requested next steps (action items):
1) Permanent fix: Patch kv-cache aggregator to limit per-shard memory growth (owner: dylan_brooks) — ETA: 2026-07-17 EOD.
2) LB policy change: Improve gradual rebalancing and add circuit-breaker for node OOM signals (owner: marcus_lin) — ETA: 2026-07-16 EOD.
3) Deployment gating: add canary memory regression tests to CI for v2.x releases (owner: grace_oconnor) — ETA: 2026-07-24.
4) Compensation/ops: propose one week of SLA credit for the impacted time window; draft note for finance and customer (owner: sean_gallagher) — ETA: 2026-07-15.

I'm preparing a 1–2 page RCA doc and will attach it to the thread shortly.

Grace O'Connor
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: BrightBay incident — exec summary & credit proposal

Hi Jason / Anika —

Appreciate the escalation and patience. For exec consumption:
- Impact: BrightBay experienced a production degradation from ~08:58–10:45 PST on 2026-07-10. Primary user-facing effect was increased latency and transient 5xxs on generation endpoints; peak throughput observed to drop ~18–22% for checkout-related flows.
- Root cause (plain): a recent service change increased memory usage on streaming cache processes; when traffic rebalanced it led to node restarts and request queuing.
- What we did: reverted the problematic change, drained/restarted affected nodes, applied a temporary routing policy, and validated traffic normalization by 10:30 PST.
- Proposed customer concessions: one week of pro-rata SLA credit (will provide exact credit amount once we finish accounting) and a weekly check‑in for 30 days to validate stability.

Action items for BrightBay sign-off:
• Accept the attached RCA (brightbay_rca_v1.pdf).
• Sign-off on the attached action tracker (action_tracker_brightbay.xlsx) which maps owners, due dates, and acceptance criteria.

I've created a short incident ticket in our tracker: RIN-8392. We'll link the Jira to the tracker so you can monitor progress. Proposed standing check-in: Tuesdays 10:00 PST starting 2026-07-20 for 4 weeks.

Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

Subject: Post-incident action plan and tracked follow-through (BrightBay)

Anika / Jason —

Following up with the formal action plan and owners (also attached as an export of the tracker):

High-level commitments:
- Permanent code fix for kv-cache aggregator memory regression (owner: dylan_brooks) — target: 2026-07-17 EOD. Acceptance: memory consumption < baseline + 5% under synthetic streaming load.
- LB rebalancing policy and OOM circuit-breaker (owner: marcus_lin) — target: 2026-07-16 EOD. Acceptance: no single-node traffic jump >10% during scale events in synthetic tests.
- Deployment gates: automated canary memory checks in CI (owner: grace_oconnor) — target: 2026-07-24.
- Customer safeguard: temporary routing rules and priority queues for checkout during high alert windows (owner: marcus_lin) — in place and active.
- SLA credit: Sean to confirm finalized credit amount by 2026-07-15 (owner: sean_gallagher).

Follow-up cadence & deliverables:
- 2026-07-15: Sean provides exact credit calculation and draft finance note (deliverable: credit_proposal.pdf).
- 2026-07-17: Dylan shares PR with unit/integration test results; Grace to run canary.
- 2026-07-20: First weekly checkpoint (10:00 PST).
- 2026-07-24: Canary memory gates in CI go live; final RCA published.

Please reply to this thread to acknowledge ownership and timelines, or propose alternate dates. Links: JIRA RIN-8392 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RIN-8392) and the tracker (https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C4D).

Evelyn Hart
